supporting_observations.claim: The repeated proxy connections in the alerted period are attributed to the same GradeBookPro updater process running as raul.diaz from C:\Users\raul.diaz\AppData\Local\GradeBookPro\gradebookproupd.exe, rather than the inventoried C:\Program Files\GradeBookPro\gradebookproupd.exe path. The process and its connection to the proxy are recorded at 13:40:54.

That process made repeated proxy-mediated HTTPS CONNECTs to update.gradebookpro.co at 13:40:54, 13:46:14, 13:50:46, 13:55:55, 14:01:05, 14:05:56, and 14:10:55. The 13:50:46 attempt received proxy status 407; the other listed attempts received status 200.

For the successful connections, endpoint network events attribute connections to the proxy to the same updater process ID 4864, corroborating that the periodic activity is not merely inferred from timing or hostname alone.

The observed executable location and destination hostname do not match the inventory’s approved GradeBookPro updater location and update.gradebookpro.com service; this discrepancy is suspicious but does not by itself establish maliciousness.

A file-create event for the same updater executable was recorded shortly after its first observed connection. The record does not establish whether this was a legitimate self-update or an unauthorized replacement.

known_telemetry_limitations: The provided network records show connections from the workstation to the explicit proxy and proxy CONNECT metadata; they do not show the HTTPS application payload for the updater sessions. Relevant records include T265-00101, T265-00115, T265-00189, T265-00220, T265-00226, and T265-00302.
The provided process and file events do not include a hash, signature, signer validation, or provenance for the per-user updater executable. Relevant records include T265-00099 and T265-00105.

The provided records do not establish who installed or launched the per-user updater, whether the .co hostname is controlled by the software vendor, or whether the updater’s activity was authorized. Relevant records include T265-00099, T265-00101, and T265-00105.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish that update.gradebookpro.co is malicious, impersonates the approved service, or is controlled by an attacker; it establishes the hostname observed in the proxy records (T265-00101, T265-00115, T265-00189, T265-00220, T265-00226, T265-00302).
The evidence does not establish whether the per-user updater is a legitimate installation, a tampered binary, or malware (T265-00099, T265-00105).
The evidence does not establish what data, if any, was sent or received within the updater’s HTTPS sessions (T265-00101, T265-00115, T265-00189, T265-00220, T265-00226, T265-00302).

The scheduled svc-grades password rotation is inventory context, but the provided records do not establish a connection between that change and the updater’s periodic traffic (T265-00099, T265-00101, T265-00336).
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire the updater executable and determine its cryptographic hash, signature, signer, origin, and relationship to the approved GradeBookPro installation.

Verify update.gradebookpro.co and the per-user installation with the GradeBookPro vendor or an authoritative internal software source; check domain registration and reputation using approved investigation sources.
Obtain full proxy and DNS/TLS telemetry for the listed sessions, including any available inspected requests, certificate details, and destination resolution.
Review endpoint file and download provenance around the updater’s execution and file-create event, including any parent process, installer, or update package records.
